land.text: 'most of the Swiss plateau at the time of their contact with the Roman Republic in the 1st century BC': the cantons between Lake Geneva, the Jura, the Rhine and the Alps' foothills

successors.note: Caesar let the Helvetii return to rebuild; Cicero's Pro Balbo (56) lists them among the foederati; Colonia Iulia Equestris was founded at Noviodunum (Nyon) between 50 and 45 BC, and Aventicum became the civitas capital under Augustus.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Helvetii row. The page has no infobox and gives no borders ('It does not give exact borders'); the eight cantons come to about 17,700 km2 by the gazetteer. Their earlier homeland in southern Germany, 'between Rhine, Main, and the Hercynian Forest' (Tacitus), was abandoned 'in the late 2nd century BC' and is not drawn. Geneva stands on the Allobroges' border.

region.text: 'most of the Swiss plateau at the time of their contact with the Roman Republic in the 1st century BC': the cantons between Lake Geneva, the Jura, the Rhine and the Alps' foothills

ledger.note: Late 2nd century BC: the Helvetii settle the Swiss plateau. The page says the Helvetii abandoned their homeland in southern Germany 'in the late 2nd century BC' and held 'most of the Swiss plateau' by the 1st; it gives no founding date, so 100 is a placeholder (page silent). The Tigurini defeated Longinus at Burdigala in 107 BC.

region.text: the country round Bibracte, 'the Aeduan oppidum' where Caesar caught up with the Helvetii; the Saône crossing lies to its east

ledger.note: 58 BC: the Helvetii march west and meet Caesar. They 'burned their homes in 58 BC', their migration began 'in March of 58 BC', and Caesar caught them crossing the Saône, where 'some three-quarters had crossed'; the fight ends 'near the Aeduan oppidum Bibracte'. The page gives no date for the Saône.

region.text: the country round Bibracte, 'the Aeduan oppidum' where Caesar caught up with the Helvetii; the Saône crossing lies to its east

ledger.note: 58 BC: Bibracte ends the migration. A Roman victory; the Helvetii and their allies 'surrender'; 'Caesar claimed only 130,000 got away, of whom 110,000 returned home'. The page gives no month (a supply timeline mentions 'around June 20').

region.text: 'most of the Swiss plateau at the time of their contact with the Roman Republic in the 1st century BC': the cantons between Lake Geneva, the Jura, the Rhine and the Alps' foothills

ledger.note: 58 BC: the Helvetii fall under Rome as an allied people. Caesar 'let the Helvetii return to rebuild their homes to defend the Rhine frontier' and Cicero's Pro Balbo (56 BC) 'lists the Helvetii among the foederati'. The land is not annexed; the Bibracte page does not give the terms, and the Helvetii 'likely lost this status in 52 BC' by supporting Vercingetorix.

ledger.note: 58 BC: the independent Helvetii end at Bibracte; the civitas lives on as a Roman ally and later a colony.

wars.name: Battle of Bibracte

zones.text: the country round Bibracte, 'the Aeduan oppidum' where Caesar caught up with the Helvetii; the Saône crossing lies to its east

wars.outcome: Roman victory: the Helvetii and their allies surrendered; Caesar claimed 130,000 got away, 110,000 of whom returned home; the Helvetii became foederati.
wars.note: The campaign began with the migration in March 58 and Caesar's blockade of the Rhone route at the Allobroges' border; the Boii and Tulingi 'arrived with 15,000 men to assist the Helvetii'.

certainty.note: The page gives no borders; the plateau between Lake Geneva, the Jura and the Rhine is the researcher's reading.

notes: New state, not in Cliopatria. Thin: no infobox, no borders, no capital before Aventicum (Augustan), so capitals is empty. Start 100 is a placeholder. The end at 58 follows roman-republic's 58 Gallic gain; the Helvetii were foederati, not subjects, so the roman-republic dossier should carry a vassal_start/vassal_end for helvetii (58-52), and its counterpart string 'Gallic tribes (Helvetii, Suebi, Belgae, Veneti, Arverni)' should name slugs. The 61 BC date for Orgetorix's conspiracy is on the Orgetorix page; the page does not date his death separately. Wikidata id left null. Family 'france' is a registry key and groups the Gallic tribes.
